$comment: RAY-CLOUD shared contract 1.0.0-rc.2. Golden fixture corpus. Every case is built deterministically from the bases below by the construction rules, then read by bundle.inspect and bundle.verify; errors[0] must match code and reason. The corpus is shared: Core and Cloud run the same bytes through the same reader.

payload/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.utf8: No third-party components are redistributed in this bundle.

payload/rayspec.yaml.utf8:
version: '1.0'
metadata:
  name: bundle-format-fixture
frontend:
  - route: /
    dir: ./assets
    spa: false

payload/migration.age.utf8: not a real age payload; inspection never decrypts

writerProfile.entryOrder: names sorted by byte value, ray.json last because every other entry starts with payload/
writerProfile.note: versionMadeBy 788 is 0x0314 (Unix, 2.0); dosDate 33 is 0x0021 (1980-01-01); externalAttributes 2175008768 is 0x81A40000 (regular file, mode 0644).

fixture.provides: every capabilities.json id with status available

testSigners.rule: A test signer key is the Ed25519 private key whose 32-byte seed is SHA-256 of the ASCII seed text. The seed texts are public, so these keys are test keys, never trusted outside tests.

order: start from the base files and manifest
files: add (utf8 or hex) or remove payload files
inventory: recompute from the resulting files (default), or keep the base inventory when inventory is "base"; names in undeclared are left out of the inventory
manifestPatch: RFC 6902 operations (add, remove, replace, copy) applied to the manifest
ray.json = canonical JSON of the manifest plus LF, unless manifestBytes replaces it
entries sorted by name bytes and written with the writer profile
archive: low-level operations applied in order

manifestBytes.replace: [old, new]: replace the first occurrence of old in the canonical ray.json; new is UTF-8 text or {hex}
manifestBytes.unsortedKeys: kind first, remaining keys in canonical order, compact, LF
manifestBytes.bom: EF BB BF followed by the canonical file

archiveOps.set: set a header field (flags, method, needed, date, ext, extra, comment, crc, csize, usize) of an entry in both headers (where both), the central record only (central) or the local header only (local)
archiveOps.addRawEntry: append an entry with the given name (or nameHex) and UTF-8 data, then re-sort all entries by name bytes
archiveOps.duplicate: write a second identical entry directly after the named one
archiveOps.move: move an entry to the given index
archiveOps.centralOffsetOf: point the central record of entry at the local header of sameAs
archiveOps.localName: write a different name (same length) in the local header only
archiveOps.prepend: write the given bytes before the first local header; central offsets are absolute file offsets
archiveOps.append: write bytes after the end record; secondArchive appends a complete strict archive with the single entry ray.json containing "{}" LF
archiveOps.zip64Record: write a ZIP64 end record and locator before the end record
archiveOps.deflate: store the entry with method 8; the stored bytes are the stream pinnedDeflateStreams records for the SHA-256 of the entry's bytes, because raw deflate output at level 9 differs between zlib builds; an entry without a pinned stream gets raw deflate level 9
archiveOps.emptyFiles: add count empty entries payload/f/NNNNN (five digits, from 00000)
archiveOps.directoryPadding: write the given bytes after the last central record and count them in the end record's central directory size

construction.readerLimits: reader limits for this case, configured downward from the defaults; the first reader step (budget) applies the larger of archiveBytes and migrationArchiveBytes for bundle.inspect and bundle.verify, archiveBytes for deploy and prepare, migrationArchiveBytes for import; after the manifest schema step the limit of the kind applies
construction.signature: a detached signature file: signerSeed names the test signer; over is this-archive or the id of another case whose bytes are signed; flipFirstByte XORs the first signature byte with 0x01
construction.trustedSignerSeeds: the test signers whose public keys the verifier trusts

decryptionCasesNote: age encryption is randomized, so these bytes are not reproducible. They are generated once with a test identity created for the corpus, committed with that identity, and checked by decrypting, not by byte comparison.
